parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
One strategy for reducing the impact of locust swarms is to hand pick individual locusts from
crops. This is done at night when the locusts are resting.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest two limitations of this strategy.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The hand‑picked locusts are crushed and dried. They are then used as animal feed.
Suggest how this can benefit farmers.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Another strategy for controlling locust swarms is spraying them with insecticide.
Describe two impacts of the overuse of insecticides.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The Emergency Locust Response Program (ELRP) is a fund of $500 million to support
countries affected by locust swarms.
Suggest ways the ELRP can support countries affected by locust swarms.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Locust populations increase after rainfall and in warm weather.
Suggest reasons why locust populations may increase in the future.

text: A student reads an internet article about a type of insect called a locust.
Locusts complete their life cycle every 8 weeks. Locusts eat crops, trees and grass.
Very large numbers of locusts in a group are called a swarm. A single swarm can
travel 145 km a day and contain up to 80 million locusts.
Locust swarms are a major threat to agriculture. One locust swarm can eat the
same amount of food per day as 35 000 people.
In April 2020, 23 countries were affected by locust swarms. Scientists stated that
of farmland in Africa was at risk from locust swarms.
